description:
The Build freeze of a map destination (Heap::map_destination_freeze) copies the entries through a temporary Vec to sort them and drop repeated keys, then writes them back. A literal whose keys are all literal atoms skips this (it is written in key order and published where it stands), so the cost falls on literals with a run-time key.

Sort and dedupe in place in the destination, then publish with the same in-place publish the key-ordered literal and the update freeze use.

Measured at the commit that introduced the key-ordered publish, instructions per literal, dev profile: a run-time-key literal 2422 on run, 3645 on interp. Moving the interpreter's run-time-key literals onto destinations cost 27% there because of this freeze, so the interpreter kept its own put chain for them (ir_interp/backend.rs, the Map arm with in_key_order false).

Done when: the run-time-key literal falls on run and on interp, measured on base and change binaries; the interpreter's second literal path is deleted and every literal builds through the destination; no pin rises. Sits at the end of the epic; does not block fz-3ul.4.
title: A map built at run time is sorted where it stands
